source.title: Transformer Circuit Faithfulness Metrics are not Robust
source.authors: Joseph Miller; Bilal Chughtai; William Saunders

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The study reevaluates the IOI circuit and argues that its measured faithfulness changes with ablation and metric choices, and that average faithfulness conceals substantial prompt-level variation.
record.gate_note: The paper evaluates the IOI circuit's faithfulness under multiple ablation settings and prompt/metric choices. The 87% result is attributed to the original IOI work, so it is not recorded as this study's own result. Results on Docstring, Sports Players, and Tracr are outside the claim versions about the IOI circuit.
record.test_reason: The study re-evaluates the existing IOI circuit in GPT-2 under varied ablation granularity, ablation value, token positions, metric aggregation, mean-ablation dataset size and name order. It reports per-prompt faithfulness. It argues the circuit's measured faithfulness reflects methodological choices as much as the circuit itself.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The authors also conclude that an optimal circuit cannot be defined from prompts alone without an evaluation methodology (shown in Tracr). They add that judging automated discovery by overlap with a ground truth found under a different ablation can mislead.
record.recipe_differences: Uses the existing IOI circuit and logit-difference-recovery measure, including node-wise mean ablation of the complement at specified token positions. It varies granularity, ablation value, token positions, prompt aggregation, name order, and mean-ablation dataset size; its mean-ablation dataset has 100 ABC prompts, unlike the roughly seven examples per template attributed to the original work.
record.method_sensitivity: Faithfulness changes with node versus edge ablation, specific versus all token positions, mean versus resample ablation, ABBA versus BABA order, ABC dataset size, and the order of averaging and percentage calculation. Per-prompt faithfulness also varies substantially.

fits_no_version.finding: In Tracr models, which edges count as the 'ground truth' circuit depends on zero versus resample ablation. Discovery methods perfectly recover the circuit when ablations are matched.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The optimal circuit for a task is undefined without specifying the ablation methodology; ablation choice changes which edges belong to the circuit.

record.problems: Most IOI condition values are presented in figures without exact numerical values in the text. The reported prompt-level variation includes extreme outliers, and the paper says plots do not show the full range of datapoints. The text reports a t-test for one comparison but gives no p-value for the edge-ablation comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Results for Docstring, Sports Players, and Tracr circuits in Sections 5 and D and Appendices D-E are not included because they do not measure the IOI circuit or the claim versions about it.

untested.parts: Head classes and roles, completeness and minimality criteria. Only overall faithfulness is re-measured.
All. No ablation of name-mover heads or backup-head analysis.
All. IOI is studied only in GPT-2. Docstring and Sports Players are different circuits, models and tasks.
No circuit-finding method is run on IOI. The claim that other ablations 'may have led them to include different edges' is an argument only.
Template-wise faithfulness, more names, and whether different components are used per name order.

record.verdict_notes: Most IOI values are figure-only, so the states rest on the text's stated comparisons. The 87% belongs to the original paper and is not this study's result. The V4 bearing is argumentative only ('may have discovered a different circuit'), so V4 is left untested. Docstring and Sports Players results show similar sensitivity but fall outside the IOI versions.

versions.untested_parts: Tests faithfulness of the existing IOI circuit, but not whether the 26 heads in 7 classes have their stated roles under patching, or whether completeness and minimality criteria are met.
The study does not ablate main name-mover heads to test whether backup heads take over.
The study does not test whether the IOI circuit or its head classes and roles recur in other models, sizes, checkpoints, or tasks.
It compares evaluation ablations and metrics for an existing circuit, but does not test whether different circuit-finding methods recover essentially the same IOI circuit.

Tests sensitivity to ablation methodology, prompt order, mean-ablation dataset size, metric calculation, and individual prompts. It does not test every possible ablation, metric, or prompt distribution.
Tests ABBA versus BABA name orders. It does not report IOI faithfulness separately across the 15 templates or test prompts with more names.

rows.subject: GPT-2

rows.note: This is the node-wise, token-specific mean-ablation condition. The plotted result is not numerically stated in the paper text; the 87% figure mentioned nearby is attributed to the original IOI work.
rows.check: This is the reference condition, the paper's replication of the original method with 100 ABC prompts. Its score is figure-only. The 87% belongs to Wang et al., not to this study.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablate the complement of the IOI circuit on a clean input, using edge ablation
rows.note: The text explicitly says the edge-level circuit with specific token positions has a median score well over 100%.
rows.check: The state cannot be a single 'observed' across both versions. For V5 the node-to-edge sensitivity is observed. For V1 a median 'well over 100%' means the circuit does not match the full model under the ablation that best fits its hypothesis, which is partial faithfulness.

source_check.correct: V1: partial correspondence to full-model behavior under this evaluation. V5: observed sensitivity to ablation granularity. The text reports a token-specific edge-ablation median well above 100%, without an exact numerical median.
source_check.problem: The shared partial state does not fit V5, for which methodological sensitivity is observed.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Mean-ablate the complement of the circuit at nodes and circuit-specific token positions; compare two ways of aggregating logit-difference recovery

conditions.value: Compute percentage for each prompt, then average

rows.baseline: Full-model logit difference under the same aggregation
rows.note: The paper says this aggregation yields substantially higher percentages than first averaging the model and ablated-model logit differences and then taking the percentage.
rows.check: Per-prompt-then-average aggregation gives substantially higher percentages than the original aggregation, so the V5 effect is observed, not partial.

source_check.correct: Figure 4 varies ABC replacement-dataset size. Under node-wise, token-specific mean ablation, averaging individual recovery percentages gives substantially higher scores than taking the ratio of average logit differences. The text does not isolate this finding to 100 ABC prompts.
source_check.problem: The fixed 100-prompt condition is transferred from Figure 3 to a Figure 4 experiment that varies dataset size.

conditions.value: Average logit differences first, then calculate percentage

rows.baseline: Full-model logit difference under the same aggregation
rows.note: This is the aggregation the paper attributes to the original IOI evaluation; the alternative per-prompt calculation gives substantially higher percentages.
rows.check: This is the reference aggregation used by the original work. It is the comparison point for R9, not an independent effect.

rows.subject: GPT-2
rows.operation_detail: Measure IOI circuit faithfulness separately for the two name orders

conditions.value: Node-wise Mean Ablation of the complement at circuit-specific token positions

rows.note: The paper says faithfulness is systematically greater for BABA prompts than ABBA prompts.
rows.check: For V5 the sensitivity to name order is observed. For V6 the circuit still recovers most of the logit difference in both orders but systematically less for ABBA, which is partial. Faithfulness differences do not show different components being used.

source_check.correct: ABC dataset size varies in Figure 4. BABA faithfulness is systematically higher than ABBA faithfulness under node-wise, token-specific mean ablation. V5: observed order sensitivity. V6: partial measured coverage across orders; different components or heuristics are not demonstrated.
source_check.problem: The text does not restrict the comparison to 100 ABC prompts, and partial does not describe the observed V5 sensitivity.

relationships.reason: Under edge-level token-specific ablation the median exceeds 100% (R5). Per-prompt faithfulness varies widely, with an IQR up to 50% and extreme outliers (R12). Faithfulness holds only on average and for particular methods.

relation.reason: Its own IOI experiments test circuit faithfulness under changes in ablation granularity, replacement values, token positions, aggregation, dataset size and name order.

tranche.reason: The study directly reevaluates the published IOI circuit and argues that its faithfulness claims require methodological and per-prompt qualifications.

source_check.notes: The paper explicitly releases AutoCircuit, so code:n should be corrected. Cross-study results and catalog counts were outside this check; the authors' methodological conclusion is supported by Sections 5-6.

statements.correction: Code released: AutoCircuit library; abstract, end of introduction, Appendix A. Node mean-versus-resample comparison: p=1e-5. Edge comparison: not statistically significant. Aggregation and name order affect recovery.
statements.problem: The empirical summary is correct. The statement accurately describes the supplied header, but that header's code:n field conflicts with the paper's explicit code release.
